record.original_question: If a polynomial M_p(T) with the properties in Question 9.3 exists, is it independent of the prime p, and is it equal to 8(g + 1)?

evidence.quote: Question 9.5 If a polynomial such as asked for in the previous question exists, is it the same for different prime numbers? Is it equal to 8(g + 1)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a prime number p. For a smooth projective geometrically irreducible curve X of genus g ≥ 2 over an algebraically closed field of characteristic p, let Aut(X) denote its automorphism group. Suppose there exists a polynomial M_p(T) ∈ ℝ[T] with the following property: for every such curve X of genus g, one has |Aut(X)| ≤ M_p(g), and this bound is sharp in a natural sense (for example, attained or asymptotically attained by some family of curves of unbounded genus).

Assuming such a polynomial M_p(T) exists for every prime p, answer the following:

(a) Is M_p(T) independent of the prime p, i.e., does there exist a single polynomial M(T) ∈ ℝ[T] such that M_p(T) = M(T) for all primes p?

(b) Is this polynomial equal to 8(T + 1)?
artifact.category_tag: Automorphism groups of curves in positive characteristic
artifact.status_search_result: The question appears in a 2004 collection of open problems on automorphisms of curves. No subsequent literature was found that settles whether the conjectured polynomial bound M_p(g) for automorphism group orders of curves in characteristic p is independent of p and equal to 8(g+1); the prior question on which this one is contingent does not appear to have been resolved.

status_evidence.title: Problems from the workshop on Automorphisms of Curves (Leiden, August 2004)
status_evidence.snippet: Collection of open problems on automorphisms of curves; includes questions on minimal maximal number of automorphisms of curves.
status_evidence.claim: The question is posed as an open problem in a workshop problem list, with no indicated resolution in the source itself.
